top_violation_types.title: Director Annual Training - Additional required topics (26 TAC §746.1311(e))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Operations director still lacked annual required training topics.

top_violation_types.title: Required Admission Information-Child's allergies and Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §744.605(15))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two children with allergies had incomplete FARE forms as they were missing one medication listed for each child by the physician.

top_violation_types.title: Posting Requirements - Daily Menu, Including All Snacks and Meals Prepared or Served (26 TAC §744.401(6))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Menu was not posted during the inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Written Activity Plans - Outline Routines and Activities (26 TAC §744.2005(b)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There were no activities observed on the tables for the children to participate in. The children were running around the cafeteria and some were fighting each other, while others sat at tables waiting.

top_violation_types.title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §744.3559(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There was not a record of monthly fire drills conducted for licensing to review.

top_violation_types.title: Report Change in Director (26 TAC §744.303(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not report a change in director.

top_violation_types.title: Franchise Tax Delinquent (26 TAC §745.247)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: According to the Texas Comptroller website, the business entity's Franchise Tax Account Status is Inactive/Forfeited. The operation is currently providing care to children with an inactive status.

top_violation_types.title: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time you hire someone (26 TAC §745.621(a)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A caregiver, with direct access to children, was present without a background check eligibility.  The caregiver was sent home during the inspection.
